harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s billing accumulator. It now sums arbitrary-size nonnegative decimal counters exactly, rejects invalid or negative records with nonzero status and no partial stdout, and persists across reboot. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced 32-bit truncation with Python arbitrary-precision integer accumulation.
Added strict record validation and deferred output until all records validate.
Preserved root:root ownership, mode 0755, and SELinux var_t context.
Removed staging, rollback, test, and bytecode artifacts.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified recovery under a changed boot identity.

evidence.requirement: Sum nonnegative decimal counters exactly, including totals above 4 GiB
evidence.summary: Verified exact outputs 4,294,967,303, 6,442,450,944, and 36,893,488,147,419,103,232 through the installed executable; tests remained successful after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Reject invalid and negative records without publishing a partial total
evidence.summary: Negative, malformed, and empty records returned nonzero status with zero stdout; post-restart invalid-input verification also passed.

evidence.requirement: Keep counters and integer-decimal output interface intact
evidence.summary: Fixture checksums remained unchanged, and bin/total.py continues accepting a counters-file argument and emitting a newline-terminated decimal integer.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed architecture, OS release, kernel, and file security metadata
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence shows RHEL 10.0 on x86_64 with the same kernel; total.py remains root:root, mode 0755, and SELinux var_t.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID 050a5b4c-6c7b-42ad-957a-b6a41a0d34db, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID d00ed025-bc77-4487-a033-338adbd65e3b, and full post-restart application/data recovery.
